Comment: CloudLab c240g5: as experiment.wiki-c1024-cloudlab-gpu-4to8-worst-copy-then-flip.json, but with its stream behind the queries: every node runs with --own-reads-first, so an old node serves the stream's reads (RAW_GET) only when its own queries leave room on the device, a few at a time (fusion/read_budget.h). A baseline, the other end of copy-then-flip's trade-off from the stream-first files: the queries keep the 4 nodes' capacity, and the flip waits until the load lets the stream through -- where the load stays above C4, until it ends and the backlog has drained. Everything else, rates included, is that file's; its Comment: CloudLab c240g5, U11's worst case: the queries are 1M of the base's own vectors, drawn without repetition (scripts/data/sample_queries.py, seed 1), so no run repeats a query and none has any locality. Ground truth for every 300th of the first 600K (fusion_gt --index: the base file is gone). Set the rates from the two worst-case capacities: Rate about 0.6 x C4 (4to8-worst-calibrate-4), RateSteps 60:exactly twice Rate, below C8 (4to8-worst-calibrate-8), the same in every protocol's file. Otherwise experiment.wiki-c1024-cloudlab-gpu-4to8-copy-then-flip.json: 4 -> 8 at 90 s under copy-then-flip. The rates here are this reservation's, from its capacities of 2026-11-21, C4 1161 and C8 2306, set by hand: Rate 850, 0.73 x C4, and at 60 s 1700, exactly twice that and 0.74 x C8, about the share of C8 the 4 -> 8 runs' step takes (0.71 on Wikipedia, 0.76 on Amazon). Without locality the reads spread evenly, so C8 is twice C4 here, and 0.6 x C4 would leave the scale-out 40% of C8 free. The same shares as 550 and 1100 from C4 742 and C8 1466.
